pages.title: What a session holds
pages.caption: A session is more than a chat. It can have its own branch, working folder, plan, diff, terminal output, browser preview and GitHub context.

pages.title: One studio, many booths
pages.caption: Three musicians, one song, each in a soundproof booth: they record apart or at the same time, and the takes are mixed later. A worktree is a booth: the same repository, but its own folder and branch.

pages.title: What’s a Git worktree?
pages.caption: A **Git worktree** is another working folder for the same repository, usually on its own branch. You can work on several tasks without stashing changes or switching branches in one folder.

pages.title: Why the app uses worktrees
pages.caption: Without isolation, tasks edit the same folder, branch state gets lost, and tests and diffs mix. With a worktree-backed session, each task gets its own folder, its branch shows in the app, and its diff stays with it, so it’s easier to inspect and approve. Sessions can run in parallel without mixing changes, but this chapter takes them one at a time.

pages.title: Where a session runs
pages.caption: Start a session with **+**, and the workspace selector below the prompt box picks where it runs: **New worktree** (its own folder and branch, the safe default), **Current checkout** (your existing clone) or **Cloud** (a cloud sandbox on GitHub’s hosted infrastructure, in public preview). **Base branch** sets where a new worktree starts. The app remembers your last choice, so switch back to **New worktree** now. A session started with **Create from** always gets a new worktree.

pages.title: Parallel sessions
pages.caption: Three crews, three channels, one spring: one repository with a worktree for each session, so their changes don’t mix. In the app you don’t dig channels. Start a session with **+** and pick **New worktree** in the workspace selector, and the app makes the folder and branch. **Current checkout** suits a quick, low-stakes look, and **Cloud** offloads the work.

pages.title: Not ports
pages.caption: Worktrees separate files and branches, not everything. Dev servers, databases and ports can still collide. The preview runs on port `5173`: for a second preview, stop one server or start the other on `5174`.

pages.title: Four flags
pages.caption: `@` brings files or folders (`@samples/book-app-web/src`), `#` issues or pull requests (`#12`), `/` slash commands (`/chronicle standup`), and `&` other sessions, when the prompt box offers it. Bring the smallest amount of useful context: less is often more.

pages.title: Drop a file on a session
pages.caption: Besides `@`, you can drag files from your computer and drop them onto a session or agent in the sidebar. It’s handy for files that aren’t in the repository.

pages.title: Slash commands
pages.caption: Type `/` in the prompt box and read the palette: commands vary by app version, plugins, skills and policy. This chapter needs two. `/chronicle standup` summarizes your last day’s work, and `/context` opens the usage popup.

pages.title: More slash commands
pages.caption: You may also see `/agent`, `/collect-debug-logs`, `/create-canvas`, `/orchestrate`, `/research`, `/review`, `/rubber-duck`, `/skills`, `/usage`, and a command for each installed skill. When in doubt, type `/` and look.

pages.title: Create from a branch
pages.caption: Point to the project in the sidebar and select the **Create from** icon. On the **Branches** tab, pick `practice-empty-state-copy`: the app starts a new session from it in a new worktree. That branch is the worktree’s base branch; the session gets a working branch of its own.

pages.title: Review the plan
pages.caption: Set **Mode** to **Plan**, type `{issue}` and pick **Improve the empty state copy**, then add the prompt below and send it. If Copilot asks about the scope first, pick the recommended answer. The plan opens in the **Plan** tab, and **Review plan** replaces the prompt box: pick **Exit plan mode and I will prompt myself**. If the **Review plan** box stays open, select **Continue**. Check that the session is back in **Interactive** before you send another prompt.
pages.code: Investigate the issue and create a plan to address it.

pages.title: Baseline, then compare
pages.caption: Send the prompt below, and the preview opens in the built-in browser panel. Search `hobbit` (**The Hobbit** appears), then `zzzz-no-match`, and note the empty state. Send `Implement the plan`, inspect the diff in the **Changes** tab or the **Changes** pill, then reload and search again: the message should now suggest changing the search term, genre or reading status.
pages.code: Run the Book App in samples/book-app-web and open the preview.

pages.title: /chronicle standup
pages.caption: Send it in the session you’ve been using. It recaps your work from the last day, and should list this session and the changes you made in it.

pages.title: /context
pages.caption: Opens the usage popup below the prompt box (or select the AI credits icon by the microphone). **Plan** is your plan’s use (**Usage hidden** in **Streamer Mode**), **Session** the AI credits used, and **Tokens** what went to the model and back. Select the **Context** bar to see how much of the context window the system prompt, tools and messages use. The categories can differ with the model and the tools in the session, and your totals will differ from the course’s picture. Check it before you add more files, issues or instructions.

pages.title: Session details
pages.caption: Select the session name at the top of the window for its working branch, base branch, **Remote control**, **Path**, **Project**, **Session name** and **Session ID**. Then ask Copilot to stop the session’s development server. No pull request needed: the practice branch has an intentional regression, and `main` already has the right behavior.

pages.title: Key takeaways
pages.caption: Sessions are focused workspaces with their own branch, diff and history. A new worktree keeps changes out of your main checkout and is the safe default. Worktrees don’t separate ports, databases or background processes, so give parallel previews different ports. `@` files and folders, `#` issues and pull requests, `/` commands.

pages.title: Your turn: light and dark
pages.caption: Add a light and dark theme to the Book App in its own worktree: start from `main` with **Create from**, attach `@samples/book-app-web/src` in **Plan** mode, then check the diff, tests and build, and `/chronicle standup`. Show the branch and worktree, the context you attached, and the change and its evidence, without changing `main`.

glossary.definition: An extra working folder for the same repository, usually checked out to its own branch.
A session gets its own folder and branch beside your clone. The safe default.
A session that runs in a cloud sandbox on GitHub’s hosted infrastructure, not your machine. In public preview.
The branch that a new worktree starts from, set in the workspace selector’s menu.
Starts a session from a branch (or other starting point). It always gets a new worktree.
Below the prompt box: where a session runs (New worktree, Current checkout or Cloud).
The content the app is using for a session: files, issues, instructions and messages.
`@` files or folders, `#` issues or pull requests, `/` slash commands, `&` other sessions.
A shortcut you type in the prompt box after `/`. Type `/` to see the palette.
Summarizes your work from the last day.
Opens the usage popup: plan, session AI credits, tokens and the context breakdown.
Below the prompt box, from `/context` or the AI credits icon: plan, session AI credits, tokens and the context breakdown.
The message an app shows when nothing matches, like the Book App with no books found.

P2.3.order.1.#.text: `#` brings issues and pull requests. A folder comes with `@`, like `@samples/book-app-web/src`.

P2.3.order.1./.text: `/` runs a command. To bring a folder, type `@`.

P2.3.order.1.&.text: `&` points at another session, not a folder. Folders come with `@`.

P2.3.order.2.@.text: `@` brings files. A recap is a slash command: `/chronicle standup`.

P2.3.order.2.#.text: `#` brings an issue. For a recap, run `/chronicle standup`.

P2.3.order.2.&.text: `&` points at a session. For your recap, run `/chronicle standup`.

P2.3.order.3.@.text: `@` brings files or folders. A bug report is an issue, and issues come with `#`.

P2.3.order.3./.text: `/` runs a command. Attach an issue with `#`, like `#12`.

P2.3.order.3.&.text: `&` points at another session. Issues come with `#`.

P2.3.order.4.@.text: `@` is for files and folders. Another session comes with `&`, when the prompt box offers it.

P2.3.order.4.#.text: `#` is for issues and pull requests. Other sessions use `&`.

P2.3.order.4./.text: `/` runs commands. Other sessions use `&`, when the prompt box offers it.

P2.3.order.5.every-folder.text: That’s the whole hold. Copilot only needs what this one fix needs. Bring the smallest amount of useful context.

P2.3.order.5.nothing.text: An empty hold isn’t useful context. Give Copilot the one thing the fix is about.

P2.3.order.5.every-issue.text: Only one issue is about this message. The rest is cargo it doesn’t need. Less is often more.

P2.3.order.6.at.text: `@` picks files and folders from your project. This letter isn’t in the repository, so drag it from your computer onto the session.

P2.3.order.6.hash.text: `#` brings issues and pull requests, not files.

P2.3.order.6.context.text: `/context` shows what the session holds. It doesn’t add a file.
